'''''Scaevola aemula''''', commonly known as the '''fairy fan-flower''' or '''common fan-flower''',<ref name="SA">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola aemula'' |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/cgi-bin/speciesfacts_display.cgi?form=speciesfacts&name=Scaevola_aemula |website=eFloraSA |publisher=State Herbarium of South Australia |access-date=28 February 2022}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Goodeniaceae]]. It has mostly egg-shaped leaves and blue, mauve or white fan-shaped flowers. It grows in New South Wales, South Australia, Victoria and Western Australia.

==Description==
''Scaevola aemula'' is a mat-forming, perennial herb that grows up to 50 cm high with brown, coarsely hairy, [[terete]] stems.  The leaves are elliptic to egg-shaped tapering near the base, [[sessile (botany)|sessile]], edges toothed, up to {{cvt|10-88|mm}} long and {{cvt|4-31|mm}} wide, decreasing in size near the flowers. The fan-shaped flowers are white, blue or mauve with a yellow centre are borne on spikes up to {{cvt|24|cm}} long, [[corolla (botany)|corolla]] {{cvt|17-25|mm}} long, flattened hairs on the outside and bearded inside and the [[Papilionaceous flower#corolla|wings]] {{cvt|1-1.5|mm}} wide. The [[bracts]] are small, leaf-like, bracteoles lance-shaped and {{cvt|4.5-7|mm}} long. Flowering occurs mostly from August to October and the fruit are a rounded, wrinkled drupe to 4.5 mm long and covered in soft, short hairs.<ref name="SA"/><ref name=NSW>{{cite web |url=https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Scaevola~aemula |title=''Scaevola aemula''|accessdate=2008-10-01 |author=|work= PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia}}</ref><ref name="FOA">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola aemula'' |url=https://profiles.ala.org.au/opus/foa/profile/Scaevola%20aemula |website=Flora of Australia |publisher=Australian Biological Resources Study, Department of Agriculture, Water and the Environment: Canberra. |access-date=28 February 2022}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Scaevola aemula'' was first formally described in 1810 by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] and the description was published in ''[[Prodromus Florae Novae Hollandiae]]''.<ref name="APNI">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola aemula'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/512876 |publisher=Australian Plant Name Index |access-date=28 February 2022}}</ref><ref name="BHL">{{cite book |last1=Brown |first1=Robert |title=Prodromus florae Novae Hollandiae et insulae Van-Diemen, exhibens characteres plantarum quas annis 1802-1805 |date=1810 |publisher= |location=London |page=584 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/29583#page/452/mode/1up |access-date=27 March 2023}}</ref> The [[botanical name|specific epithet]] (''aemula'') means "striving after".<ref name="Sharr">{{cite book |last1=Sharr |first1=Francis Aubi |last2=George |first2=Alex |title=Western Australian Plant Names and Their Meanings |date=2019 |publisher=Four Gables Press |location=Kardinya, WA |isbn=9780958034180 |page=128 |edition=3rd}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Fairy fan-flower grows in dry sclerophyll forest mostly on sandy soils from the [[Eyre Peninsula]] in [[South Australia]], through [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]] to [[Mount Warning]] in [[New South Wales]] and in the [[Esperance Plains]] bioregion of [[Western Australia]].<ref name="FOA"/><ref name=FB>{{FloraBase|name=''Scaevola aemula''|id=7594}}</ref> It also occurs in the [[Great Oyster Bay]] region between the [[Prosser River]] and [[Apsley River (Tasmania)|Apsley River]] in [[Tasmania]].<ref name="dpipwe">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola aemula'' |url=https://nre.tas.gov.au/Documents/Scaevola-aemula.pdf |publisher=Tasmanian Government, Department of Primary Industries, Parks, Water and Environment |access-date=7 February 2026}}</ref><ref name="Telopea 9(2)">{{cite journal |last1=Rozefelds |first1=Andrew Carl Frank |title=The species of ''Scaevola'' (Goodeniaceae) in Tasmania |journal=Telopea |date=2001 |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=348–350 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/265476#page/130/mode/1up |access-date=7 February 2026}}</ref>

==Conservation status==
''Scaevola aemula'' is listed as "endangered" under the Tasmanian Government ''[[Threatened Species Protection Act 1995]]''.<ref name="dpipwe" />

==Use in horticulture==
The species is thought to be the most commonly cultivated of the genus ''[[Scaevola (plant)|Scaevola]]'', and a large number of cultivars have been developed. Most of these are mat-forming to a height of 12 cm and spreading up to 1 metre in width. It prefers a sunny or partially shaded, well-drained position and tolerates salt spray and periods of drought. Pruning and pinching of tip growth may be carried out to shape the plant. Propagation is from cuttings or by [[layering (horticulture)|layering]].<ref name="ANPSA">{{cite web |title=''Scaevola aemula'' |url=https://anpsa.org.au/plant_profiles/scaevola-aemula/ |website=Plant Guides |publisher=Australian Native Plants Society (Australia) |access-date=11 October 2025 }}</ref><ref name=Seale>{{cite book|author=Seale, Alan| title=Garden Companion to Native Plants| publisher=Reed Books|location=Australia | year=1988 | isbn=0730101878}}</ref>
